body.text: śrī vasudhārādhāraṇī |
om namaḥ | śrī jinaśāsanāya |

evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān kośāmbyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ kaṇṭakasaṃjñake mahāvanavare ghositārāme mahābhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ pañcamātrairbhikṣuśataissaṃvarabahulaiśca tapodhanairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvaśuddhadharmaguṇasamanugataiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma |

tena punaḥ khalu samayena kauśāmbyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ sucandro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati sma | upaśāntendriya upaśāntamānaso bahupoṣyo bahuputro bahuduhitṛko bahubhṛtyaparijanasampannaḥ śrāddho mahāśrāddhaḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ [yena] bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ anekaśatasahasrapradakṣaṇīkṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdat | ekānte niṣaṇṇaśca sucandro gṛhapatirlabdhāvasaro bhagavantametadavocat |

pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgataṃ arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kiñcit pradeśaṃ sacet me bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya | evamukte bhagavān sucandraṃ gṛhapatimetadavocat | pṛccha tvaṃ gṛhapate yadyadevākāṃkṣasi, ahaṃ te yathāpraśnavyākaraṇāya cittamārādhayiṣye | evamukte sucandro gṛhapatiḥ sādhu bhagavanniti kṛtvā bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhagavantametadavocat |

kathaṃ bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daridro bhūtvā adaridro bhavati vyādhitaśca bhūtvā avyādhito bhavati | atha khalu bhagavān jānanneva sucandraṃ gṛhapatimetadavocat | kimiti tvaṃ [gṛhapate daridratāyāḥ paripraśnaṃ pṛcchasi evamukte] gṛhapatirbhagavantaṃ etadavocat | daridro 'haṃ bhagavan daridro 'haṃ sugata bahupoṣyo bahuputro bahuduhitṛko bahubhṛtyaparijanasaṃpannaśca | taddarśayatu bhagavāṃstādṛśaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ yena daridrāḥ sattvāḥ adaridrāḥ bhaveyuḥ vyādhitāśca sattvā avyādhitā bhaveyuḥ bahudhanadhānyakośakoṣṭāgārasampannāśca bhaveyuḥ priyā manāpāśca manojñāḥ saṃdarśanīyāśca bhaveyuḥ dānapatayo mahādānapatayaśca akṣīṇahiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyaratnakośakoṣṭāgārāśca bhaveyuḥ | maṇimuktāvaiḍūryavajraśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatasamṛddhāśca bhaveyuḥ | supratiṣṭhitasusamṛddhagṛhaputradārakuṭumbāśca bhaveyuḥ |

evamukte bhagavān sucandragṛhapatimetadavocat | asti gṛhapate teṣvapi asaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣvatīteṣu pramāṇeṣu yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayena bhagavān vajradharasāgaranirghoṣo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpāta(di) vidyācaraṇasampanno lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tasya tathāgatasyāntikānmayā gṛhapate ayaṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇī śrutā śrutvā copagṛhītā dhāritā vācitā paryavāptā pravarttitā prakīrttitā anumoditā parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśitā ahamapyetarhi gṛhapate tāṃ dhāriṇīṃ bhāṣiṣye yathā asyā dhāriṇyāḥ prabhāvena kulaputraṃ mānuṣā na viheṭhayanti amānuṣāḥ ... yakṣāḥ ... rākṣasāḥ ... pretāḥ ... piśācā ... bhūtā ... kumbhāṇḍā ... (

children.text: ) skandā ... apasmārā ... ustā ... pūtanā ... kaṭapūtanā ... yātudhānā na viheṭhayanti | mūtrāhārā rūdhirāhārā viṣṭāhārā vasāhārā māṃsāhārā śleṣmāhārā pūāhārā siṃhāṇakāhārā khelāhārā medhāhārā madyāhārā jātāhārā jīvitāhārā balyāhārā mālyāhārā yāvaducchiṣṭāhārā na viheṭhayanti | yasya ceyaṃ gṛhapate dhāriṇī śrāddhasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā hṛdayagatā hastagatā śrutimātragatā paryavāptā pravarttitā prakīrtitā viciṃtitā dhāritā vācitā likhitā anumoditā parebhyaśca saṃprakāśitā ca bhaviṣyati tasya kulaputrasya kuladuhiturvā dīrgharātraṃ arthāya sukhāya hitāya kṣemāya subhikṣāya yogasaṃbhārāya bhaviṣyati | yaścaimāṃ vasudhārādhāriṇīṃ tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo mahatīṃ udārāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā namaskṛtvā arcayet ardharātreścaturvārān tasya devatā āttamanaskāḥ pramuditāḥ prītāḥ saumanasyajātāstvayamevāgatya dhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇaratnavṛṣṭiṃ pātayiṣyanti tāḥ prītāstathāgataśāsane prītā buddhaprajñaptyā prītā saṃghaprajñaptyā prītā mama dharmabhāṇakasyāśayena ca | namo ratnatrayāya | om namo bhagavate vajradharasāgaranirghoṣāya tathāgatasyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya tadyathā om śrī surūpe suvadane bhadre subhadre bhadravati maṃgale sumaṃgale maṃgalavati argale argalavati candre candravati ale acale acapale udghātini udbhedini ucchedini udyotini śasyavati dhanavati dhānyavati udyotavati śrīmati prabhavati amale vimale nirmale rurume surūpe surupavimale arcanaste atanaste vitanaste anunaste (?) avanatahaste viśvakeśi viśvaniśi viśvanaṃśi viśvarūpiṇi viśvanakhi viśvaśire viśuddhaśīle vigūhanīye viśuddhanīye uttare anuttare aṃkure naṃkure prabhaṃkure rarame ririme rurume khakhame khikhime khukhume dhadhame dhidhime dhudhume tatare tatare ture ture tara tara tāraya tāraya māṃsarvasattvāṃśca vajre vajre vajragarbhe vajropame vajriṇi vajravati ukke bukke nukke dhukke kakke hakke ḍhakke ṭakke varakke āvarttini nivarttini nivarṣaṇi pravarṣaṇi vardhani pravardhani niṣpādani vajradharasāgaranirghoṣaṃ tathāgataṃ anusmara anusmara sarvatathāgatasatyamanusmara saṃghasatyamanusmara anihāri anihāri tapa tapa kuṭa kuṭa pūra pūra pūraya pūraya bhagavati vasudhāre mama saparivārasya sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ ca bhara bhara bharaṇi (
children.translated_text: ) <s>skandas</s> (seizure-spirits)... <s>apasmāras</s> (epilepsy-spirits)... <s>ustas</s>... <s>pūtanās</s> (putrid-spirits)... <s>kaṭapūtanās</s> (foul-corpse spirits)... <s>yātudhānas</s> (sorcerers) cannot cause harm. Those who feed on urine, those who feed on blood, those who feed on excrement, those who feed on fat, those who feed on flesh, those who feed on phlegm, those who feed on pus, those who feed on mucus, those who feed on saliva, those who feed on marrow, those who feed on liquor, those who feed on birth-substances, those who feed on life-force, those who feed on offerings, those who feed on garlands, and even those who feed on leftovers — none of them can cause harm. O householder, for the faithful son of good family or daughter of good family in whose heart this <s>dhāraṇī</s> has entered, in whose hand it has come, who has merely heard it, who has received it, set it in motion, proclaimed it, contemplated it, retained it, recited it, written it, rejoiced in it, and made it known to others — for that son or daughter of good family, it will be for their long-lasting benefit, happiness, welfare, security, abundance, and accumulation of the requisites of <s>yoga</s>. And whoever, having made a great and magnificent offering to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the worthy ones (<s>arhats</s>), the perfectly awakened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>), and having paid homage, worships this <s>Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī</s> four times at midnight — the deities, joyful, delighted, pleased, filled with gladness, will come of their own accord and cause a rain of wealth, grain, silver, gold, and jewels to fall. They are pleased with the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, pleased with the designation of the <s>Buddha</s>, pleased with the designation of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and pleased with the intention of me, the preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatrayāya</s>)! Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One <s>Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa</s> (Vajra-Holder Whose Voice is Like the Ocean's Roar), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Thus: Oṃ, O Glorious One, O Beautiful-Formed, O Fair-Faced, O Auspicious, O Supremely Auspicious, O Blessed with Auspiciousness, O Auspicious, O Supremely Auspicious, O Endowed with Auspiciousness, O Bolt, O Bolt-Bearer, O Lunar, O Moon-Endowed, O Graceful, O Immovable, O Unshakable, O Uprooter, O Breaker-Through, O Cutter-Off, O Illuminator, O Grain-Bearer, O Wealth-Bearer, O Grain-Endowed, O Radiant, O Glorious, O Mighty, O Stainless, O Spotless, O Immaculate, rurume surūpe surupavimale arcanaste atanaste vitanaste anunaste avanatahaste, O Universal-Haired, O Universal-Eyed, O Universal-Limbed, O Universal-Formed, O Universal-Nailed, O Universal-Headed, O Pure-Virtued, O Worthy-of-Concealment, O Worthy-of-Purification, O Supreme, O Unsurpassed, O Sprout, O Jewel-Sprout, O Radiant-Sprout, rarame ririme rurume khakhame khikhime khukhume dhadhame dhidhime dhudhume, cross over, cross over, save, save, deliver, deliver — deliver me and all beings! O <s>Vajra</s>, O <s>Vajra</s>, O <s>Vajra</s>-Essence, O <s>Vajra</s>-Like, O <s>Vajra</s>-Bearer, O <s>Vajra</s>-Endowed, ukke bukke nukke dhukke kakke hakke ḍhakke ṭakke varakke, O Turner, O Reverser, O Rain-Ceaser, O Rain-Bringer, O Increaser, O Promoter, O Accomplisher — remember, remember the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa</s>! Remember the truth of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Remember the truth of the <s>Saṅgha</s>! Unyielding, unyielding, blaze, blaze, crush, crush, fill, fill, fulfill, fulfill! O Blessed <s>Vasudhārā</s> (Stream of Wealth), sustain, sustain me together with my retinue and all beings, O Sustainer (

children.text: ) śāntamati jayamati mahāmati sumaṃgalamati piṃgalamati subhadramati śubhamati candramati āgacchāgaccha samayamanusmara svāhā | svabhāvāmanusmara svāhā | dhṛtiṃ .... | sarvatathāgatānāṃ vinayaṃ ... hṛdayaṃ ... upahṛdayaṃ ... jayaṃ ... vijayaṃ ... sarvasatvavijayamanusmara svāhā |
children.translated_text: ) O <s>Śāntamati</s> (Peaceful-Minded), O <s>Jayamati</s> (Victorious-Minded), O <s>Mahāmati</s> (Great-Minded), O <s>Sumaṅgalamati</s> (Well-Auspicious-Minded), O <s>Piṅgalamati</s> (Tawny-Minded), O <s>Subhadramati</s> (Greatly-Auspicious-Minded), O <s>Śubhamati</s> (Beautiful-Minded), O <s>Candramati</s> (Moon-Minded), come, come! Remember the vow, <s>svāhā</s>! Remember one's own nature, <s>svāhā</s>! Steadfastness... The discipline of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>... the heart... the subsidiary heart... victory... complete victory... remember the victory over all beings, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: om śrīṃ vasumukhīṃ svāhā | om śrīṃ vasuśrī svāhā | om śrīṃ vasuśriye svāhā | om vasumati svāhā | om vasumatiśriye svāhā | om vasve svāhā | om vasude svāhā | om vasuṃdhari svāhā | om dhariṇi dhāriṇi svāhā | om samayasaumye samayaṃkari mahāsamaye svāhā | om śriye svāhā | om śrīkari svāhā | om dhanakari svāhā | om dhānyakari svāhā |
body.translated_text: Oṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Vasumukhī</s> (Wealth-Faced), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Vasuśrī</s> (Wealth-Glory), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ śrīṃ, to <s>Vasuśrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to <s>Vasumati</s> (Wealth-Minded), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to <s>Vasumatiśrī</s> (Glory of Wealth-Mind), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to Wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the Giver of Wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to <s>Vasuṃdharī</s> (Bearer of Wealth), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the Upholder, to the Bearer, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, O Gentle-of-Vow, O Vow-Maker, O Great-Vow, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to Śrī (Fortune), <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the Maker of Fortune, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the Maker of Wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! Oṃ, to the Maker of Grain, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: mūlamantra | om śriye śrīkari svāhā | om dhanakari dhānyakari ratnavarṣaṇi svāhā | sādhyamantra | om vasudhāre svāhā | hṛdayam | lakṣmyai svāhā | om upahṛdayam | om lakṣmī bhūtalanivāsine svāhā | saṃyathā daṃ om yānapātrāvahe svāhā | mā dūragāminī anutpannānāṃ dravyāṇāmutpādini utpannānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ vṛddhiṃkari truṭe liṭe liṭe li ita ita āgacchāgaccha bhagavati mā vilambaṃ manorathaṃ me paripūraya | daśabhyo digbhyo yathodakadhārā paripūrayanti mahīṃ yathā tamāṃsi bhāskaro raśminā vidhyāpayati ciraṃtanāni yathā śaśī śītāṃśunā niṣpādayatyauṣadhīḥ |
body.translated_text: The root <s>mantra</s>: <s>Oṃ śriye śrīkari svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ dhanakari dhānyakari ratnavarṣaṇi svāhā</s>! The accomplishment <s>mantra</s>: <s>Oṃ vasudhāre svāhā</s>! The heart [<s>mantra</s>]: <s>Lakṣmyai svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ</s> — the subsidiary heart: <s>Oṃ lakṣmī bhūtalanivāsine svāhā</s>! Thus: <s>Oṃ yānapātrāvahe svāhā</s>! O you who do not go far, who generate things not yet arisen and increase things already arisen! <s>Truṭe liṭe liṭe li ita ita</s> — come, come, O Blessed One! Do not delay — fulfill my heart's desire! Just as streams of water fill the earth from the ten directions, just as the sun with its rays dispels ancient darkness, just as the moon with its cool rays ripens the herbs —

children.translated_text: always contemplate accomplishment that follows the mind's desire for humans,
so may these [<s>mantras</s>], constantly contemplated by me according to my wish,
and all <s>mantra</s>-words, be accomplished through effort!

body.text: tadyathā | suṭa suṭa khaṭa khaṭa khiṭi khiṭi khuṭu khuṭu maru maru muṃca muṃca maruñca maruñca tarppiṇi tarppiṇi tarjani tarjani dehi dehi dāpaya dāpaya uttiṣṭa uttiṣṭa hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ pradāpaya svāhā | annapānāya svāhā | vasunipātāya svāhā | gauḥ svāhā surabhe svāhā | vasu svāhā | vasupataye svāhā | indrāya svāhā | yamāya svāhā | varuṇāya svāhā | vaiśravaṇāya svāhā | digbhyo vidigbhyaḥ svāhā | utpādayantu me kāṃkṣāvirahaṃ anumodayantu imaṃ me mantrapadāḥ | om hraṃ hrīṃ ehyehi bhagavati dada dāpaya svāhā | etadbhagavatyā āryavasudhārāyā hṛdayaṃ mahāpāpakariṇo 'pi siddhyati puruṣapramāṇān svabhogān dadāti īpsitaṃ manorathaṃ paripūrayati kāmaduhān yān kāmān kāmayati tāṃstānīpsitān paripūrayati | mūlavidyā | namo ratnatrayāya | namo devi dhanadaduhite vasudhāre dhanadhārāṃ pātaya kuru 2 dhaneśvarī dhanade ratnade he hemadhanaratnasāgaramahānidhāne nidhānakoṭiśatasahasraparivṛte ehyehi bhagavati praviśya matpuraṃ madbhavane mahādhanadhānyadhārāṃ pātaya kuru 2 om hraṃ traṭa kailāsavāsinīye svāhā | mahāvidyā | om vasudhāre mahāvṛṣṭinipātini vasu svāhā | mūlahṛdayaṃ | om vasudhāre sarvārthasādhinī sādhaya 2 uddhara 2 rakṣa 2 | sarvārthanidhayantraṃ vava ṭata vava ṭaṇṭa ḍaṇḍa svāhā | paramahṛdayaṃ | om namo bhagavatyai āryalevaḍike yathā jīvasaṃrakṣaṇi phalahaste divyarūpe dhanade varade śuddhe viśuddhe śivakari śāntikari bhayanāśini bhayadūṣaṇi sarvaduṣṭān bhañjaya 2 mohaya 2 jambhaya 2 stambhaya 2 mama śāntiṃ puṣṭiṃ vaśyaṃ rakṣāṃ ca kuru 2 svāhā | levaḍikā dhāriṇīyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Namely: <s>suṭa suṭa khaṭa khaṭa khiṭi khiṭi khuṭu khuṭu maru maru muñca muñca maruñca maruñca tarppiṇi tarppiṇi tarjani tarjani dehi dehi dāpaya dāpaya uttiṣṭa uttiṣṭa</s> — cause gold and riches to be given, <s>svāhā</s>! For food and drink, <s>svāhā</s>! For the descent of wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! To the cow, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Surabhi</s> (the wish-fulfilling cow), <s>svāhā</s>! To wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! To the lord of wealth, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Yama</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), <s>svāhā</s>! To the cardinal and intermediate directions, <s>svāhā</s>! May they generate for me the removal of want and may they rejoice in these my <s>mantra</s>-words! <s>Oṃ hraṃ hrīṃ ehyehi bhagavati dada dāpaya svāhā</s>! This is the heart of the Blessed Noble <s>Vasudhārā</s>. It is accomplished even for one who has committed great sins — it bestows enjoyments the measure of a person, fulfills desired wishes, and like a wish-fulfilling cow, whatever desires one desires, it fulfills all those wishes. The root <s>vidyā</s>: Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the Goddess, daughter of <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera), <s>Vasudhārā</s>! Cause a stream of wealth to rain down! Bestow, bestow, O Goddess of Wealth! O giver of riches, O giver of jewels! O great treasury of gold, riches, jewels, and ocean! Surrounded by ten million hundred-thousand treasuries — come, come, O Blessed One, enter my city, my dwelling, and cause a great stream of wealth and grain to rain down! Bestow, bestow! <s>Oṃ hraṃ traṭa kailāsavāsinīye svāhā</s>! The great <s>vidyā</s>: <s>Oṃ vasudhāre mahāvṛṣṭinipātini vasu svāhā</s>! The root-heart: <s>Oṃ vasudhāre sarvārthasādhinī sādhaya sādhaya uddhara uddhara rakṣa rakṣa</s>! The <s>yantra</s> (diagram) for accomplishing all purposes: <s>vava ṭata vava ṭaṇṭa ḍaṇḍa svāhā</s>! The supreme heart: <s>Oṃ</s> — homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Levaḍikā</s>! O you who protect life, with fruit in hand, of divine form, giver of riches, bestower of boons, pure, supremely pure, creator of auspiciousness, creator of peace, destroyer of fear, dispeller of fear! Crush, crush all the wicked! Delude, delude! Paralyze, paralyze! Immobilize, immobilize! Create for me peace, nourishment, subjugation, and protection! <s>Svāhā</s>! This is the <s>Levaḍikā</s> dhāraṇī.

body.text: iyaṃ sā gṛhapate imāni vasudhārādhāriṇīmantrapadāni sarvatathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā ṣaṇmāsānnāvartayet tataḥ siddhā bhavati yasmiṃśca sthāne iyaṃ mahāvidyā vācyate sā dik pūjyamānā (

children.text: ) bhavati pauṣṭikakāryaṃ svagṛhe paragṛhe vā bhagavatastathāgatasyāryāvalokiteśvarasya ca mantradevatāyāścāgrataḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyo namaskṛtvā śubhe sthāne kośe koṣṭāgāre vā candanena caturasramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā trīn vārān āvartayan tato gṛhapate kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā mahāpuruṣamātrayā vasudhārayā gṛhaṃ paripūrayati sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇaratnaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiśca sarvopadravāṃśca nāśayati | tena hi tvaṃ gṛhapate udgṛgṛhīṣvemāṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇīṃ dhāraya vācaya deśaya udgrāhaya paryavāpnuhi pravartaya anumodaya parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya tad bhaviṣyati dīrgharātraṃ arthāya hitāya subhikṣāya kṣemāya yogasambhārāya ceti |
children.translated_text: ) For the performance of prosperity rites, whether in one's own house or another's house, one should make obeisance to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas before the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, and the <s>mantra</s>-deity. In an auspicious place, a treasury, or a storehouse, having made a square <s>maṇḍala</s> with sandalwood and revolving three times, then, O householder, <s>Vasudhārā</s> fills the house of the son of good family or the daughter of good family to the measure of a great person with all wealth, grain, silver, gold, jewels, and all provisions, and destroys all calamities. Therefore, O householder, take up this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s> — retain it, recite it, teach it, master it, comprehend it, propagate it, rejoice in it, and proclaim it widely to others. That will be for long-lasting benefit, welfare, abundance, security, and the accumulation of spiritual merit.

body.translated_text: This, O householder, is it. Having worshipped all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, one should recite these <s>Vasudhārādhāraṇī</s> <s>mantra</s>-words for six months — then it becomes accomplished. And in whatever place this great <s>vidyā</s> is recited, that direction, being honored (

body.text: sādhu bhagavanniti sucandro gṛhapatiḥ bhagavato 'ntikādimāṃ vasudhārāṃ nāma dhāriṇīṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya kṛtakarapuṭo bhūtvā bhagavantametadavocat | udgṛhītā me bhagavan iyaṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇī prakīrtitā dhāritā vācitā paryavāptā anumoditā manasānupariciṃtitā ca parebhyaśca vistareṇa idānīṃ samprakāśayiṣyāmīti |
body.translated_text: "Excellent, O Blessed One!" said <s>Sucandra</s> the householder. Having heard this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s> from the Blessed One, delighted, pleased, elated, joyful, gladdened, and filled with delight and happiness, he fell at the feet of the Blessed One, and with palms joined together, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "I have received, O Blessed One, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>. It has been proclaimed, retained, recited, comprehended, rejoiced in, and contemplated in my mind. And now I shall proclaim it widely to others."

body.text: atha tatkṣaṇamātreṇa sucandro nāma gṛhapati[ḥ] paripūrṇakośakoṣṭāgāro babhūva | atha khalu sucandro gṛhapatiḥ bhagavantaṃ anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ anekaśaḥ punaḥ punaravalokya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, at that very instant, the householder <s>Sucandra</s>'s treasuries and storehouses became full. Then the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, having circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and having looked back at the Blessed One again and again, departed from the presence of the Blessed One.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantrayate sma | gaccha tvaṃ ānaṃda sucandrasya gṛhapateragāraṃ gatvā ca paripūrṇaṃ paśya sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyaratnasuvarṇaiḥ sarvopakaraṇairmahākośakoṣṭāgārāṇi ca paripūrṇāni |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to the house of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, and see it filled with all wealth, grain, silver, jewels, gold, all provisions, and the great treasuries and storehouses full."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān ānaṃdo bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yena kośāmbīmahānagarī yena sucandrasya gṛhapateragāraṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramyābhyantaraṃ praviśyādrākṣīt tat paripūrṇaṃ sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiśca (

children.text: ) mahākośakoṣṭāgārāṇi ca paripūrṇāni | dṛṣṭvā ca vismito hṛṣṭaḥ santuṣṭaḥ udagra āttamanā pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto yena bhagavāṃstena upasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivaṃdya bhagavantametadavocat | ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo 'sya yena sucandro gṛhapatirmahādhano mahābhogo mahākośakoṣṭāgāraḥ sarvadhanadhānyasamṛddhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | bhagavānāha | śrāddhānaṃda sucandragṛhapatiḥ paramaśrāddhaḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ | udgṛhītā ca teneyaṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇī dhāritā vācitā deśitā grāhitā paryavāptā prakīrtitā anumoditā idānīṃ parebhyaśca saṃprakāśayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: ) and the great treasuries and storehouses full. Having seen this, amazed, delighted, contented, elated, joyful, gladdened, and filled with delight and happiness, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he spoke thus to the Blessed One: "What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder <s>Sucandra</s> has become one of great wealth, great fortune, great treasuries and storehouses, and abundant in all wealth and grain?" The Blessed One said: "The householder <s>Sucandra</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, is faithful, supremely devoted, and of virtuous intention. He has received this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>, retained it, recited it, taught it, caused others to receive it, comprehended it, proclaimed it, rejoiced in it, and will now proclaim it widely to others."

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, approached the great city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> and the house of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>. Having approached and entered within, he saw it full of all wealth, grain, silver, gold, and all provisions,

body.text: tena cānaṃda tvamapyudgṛhīṣvemāṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇīṃ dhāraya vācaya deśaya grāhaya paryavāpnuhi pravarttaya prakīrtaya anumodaya parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya | yasyeyaṃ kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā hastagatā gṛhagatā pustakagatā bhaviṣyati na tasya rogadurbhikṣamarakakāṃtārādayo bhaviṣyanti krameṇa vibhavāstasya pravardhiṣyanti tad bhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: "Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you too should take up this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s> — retain it, recite it, teach it, cause others to receive it, comprehend it, propagate it, proclaim it, rejoice in it, and proclaim it widely to others. For whichever son of good family or daughter of good family has this in their hands, in their home, or in a manuscript, they will not experience disease, famine, pestilence, or dangers of the wilderness. Gradually their prosperity will increase. That will be for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare and happiness of the great multitude of beings, both gods and humans."

body.text: nāhaṃ ānaṃda taṃ dharme samanupaśyāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāṃ ca imāṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇīṃ mahāvidyāṃ anyathā kariṣyati atikramiṣyati vā naitatsthānaṃ vidyate | tat kasya hetoḥ | abhedyā hyete ānaṃda vasudhārādhāriṇīmantrā na vaite kṣīṇakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ śrutipatha[mapyā]gamiṣyanti kaḥ punarvādo pustakagatāmapi kṛtvā gṛhe (

children.text: ) dhārayiṣyanti | tat kasya hetoḥ | sarvatathāgatānāṃ hyetad vākyaṃ sarvatathāgataireṣā dhāriṇī bhāṣitā adhiṣṭhitā svamudrikayā mudritā prabhāvitā prakāśitā prakīrtitā anumoditā praśastā saṃvartitā vivṛtottānīkṛtā ārocitā svākhyātā sunirdiṣṭā ca sarvasattvānāṃ daridrāṇāṃ nānāvyādhiparipīḍitānāṃ sarvaduṣṭabhayopadravāṇāṃ cārthāyeti |
children.translated_text: keep them. Why is that? Because this is the word of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This <s>dhāraṇī</s> has been spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, empowered, sealed with their own seal, made powerful, illuminated, proclaimed, approved, praised, set in motion, revealed and elucidated, announced, well-explained, and well-taught — for the benefit of all beings who are poor, afflicted by various diseases, and [troubled by] all hostile fears and calamities.

body.translated_text: I do not see, <s>Ānanda</s>, anyone in this world — with its <s>devas</s>, <s>Māra</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>, among the generations of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> — who could alter or transgress this great <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>. There is no such possibility. Why is that? Because these <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>mantras</s> are indestructible, <s>Ānanda</s>. They will not even reach the hearing of beings whose roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are exhausted — how much less will such beings write them down and keep them in their homes

body.text: ānanda āha | udgṛhītā me bhagavanniyaṃ vasudhārā nāma dhāriṇī dhāritā vācitā grāhitā deśitā pravarttitā prakīrtitā anumoditā manasā supariciṃtitā |
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Blessed One, I have grasped this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>, retained it, recited it, mastered it, taught it, set it in motion, proclaimed it, approved it, and thoroughly contemplated it in my mind.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān ānaṃda utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ kṛtakarapuṭo bhūtvā idamudānayati sma |
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and bowing with joined palms toward the Blessed One, at that moment, with cupped hands, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Inconceivable is the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, inconceivable too is the <s>Buddhadharma</s>,
inconceivable indeed is the ripening [of karma] for beings here, and inconceivable too [is the result].
Come, O All-knowing Teacher, who has crossed beyond old age and death,
O <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), O attainer of the fruit, homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s>-hero!

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān ānaṃdo hṛṣṭa tuṣṭa āttamanā pramuditā prītisaumanasyajāto bhagavantametadavocat | ko nāma bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ kaścemāṃ dhārayāmi | bhagavānāha | tena hi tvamānaṃda sucandragṛhapatiparipṛcchetyapi dhāraya sarvadhanadhānyamityapi dhāraya sarvatathāgatapraśarato vasudhārādhāriṇīkalpaṃ ityapi dhāraya |
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, delighted, pleased, elated, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, said to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the name of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), and how should I retain it?' The Blessed One replied: 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain it as "The Inquiry of the Householder <s>Sucandra</s>," retain it also as "All Wealth and Grain," and retain it also as "The Ritual Manual of the <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>Dhāraṇī</s> from the Delight of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>."'

body.text: idamavocad bhagavannāttamanā āyuṣmān ānaṃdaste ca bhikṣavaste ca bodhisatvā sā sarvāvatī parṣad sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvāśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanaṃdanniti |
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The elated Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those <s>bhikṣus</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

body.text: ityāryavasudhārādhāriṇī samāptā || cha || cha || cha || saṃvat 1695 varṣe aśvana vadi 7 bhṛguvāsare || cha || cha || cha || sāhaśrī pamanīyāsuta sāhaśrī indrajī suṃdara paṭhanārthe paropakārārtham || śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭakayoḥ || || śrī ||
body.translated_text: Thus the Noble <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>Dhāraṇī</s> is complete. In the year <s>Saṃvat</s> 1695, on the 7th of the dark half of <s>Āśvina</s>, on a Friday. For the reading of <s>Sāhaśrī Pamanīyā</s>'s son <s>Sāhaśrī Indrajī Sundara</s>, for the benefit of others. May there be auspiciousness for the scribe and the reader. <s>Śrī</s>.
